sentences.en: The son is going to work in the north, and mom helps him pack his suitcase.
Mom said: "It's cold in the north, you need to wear more clothes and take care of your health."
At the train station, mom still felt a little worried, and kept looking at her son.
The train was about to leave, and the son, holding his suitcase, said to his mother: "Mom, I'm heading off."
Mom said: "Call me once you arrive, look after yourself well, take care!"
The son said: "Mom, take care too, and don't worry about me."
The train pulled away, and his mother stood there watching it until she couldn't see it any more.

quiz.q: Why is the son leaving home?
a: He is going to work in the north
He is moving in with a friend

quiz.q: What does the mother tell her son to do before he leaves?
a: Wear more clothes and take care of his health

quiz.q: What does the son say back to his mother?
a: That she should take care too and stop worrying
That he wants to stay home

grammar.e: 保重 is a warmer send-off than 再见 — it's used when someone is going away for a while, and wishes them wellbeing rather than just saying goodbye.
grammar.x: 妈妈，你也要保重。— Mom, take care of yourself too.

grammar.p: V + 着（an action held in progress）
grammar.e: 着 after a verb shows the action continuing, often while something else happens at the same time.
grammar.x: 妈妈一直看着儿子。— Mom kept looking at her son.

grammar.e: Repeating a verb with 着 twice shows an action going on until something changes as a result.
grammar.x: 看着看着，就看不见了。— She watched and watched, until she couldn't see it anymore.
